goal_text: How to choose between RAG and fine-tuning

nodes.title: What RAG and fine-tuning actually do
nodes.one_liner: The core difference: retrieving facts vs. reshaping the model itself.

nodes.title: Which problem are you actually solving?
nodes.one_liner: Matching each approach to knowledge vs. behavior/style goals.

nodes.title: How often does your information change?
nodes.one_liner: Why freshness and update frequency favor one approach.

nodes.title: What data do you have to work with?
nodes.one_liner: Documents to retrieve vs. labeled examples to train on.

nodes.title: Cost, latency, and maintenance trade-offs
nodes.one_liner: Ongoing effort, response speed, and money over time.

nodes.title: Accuracy, traceability, and hallucination control
nodes.one_liner: Which gives citable sources and fewer made-up answers.

nodes.title: When to combine both
nodes.one_liner: Cases where RAG plus fine-tuning beats either alone.

nodes.title: A decision checklist for your project
nodes.one_liner: Questions to answer to reach a confident choice.

outline.rationale: The user is new to both approaches but deciding for a real project, so I ground the two concepts lightly in one node, then focus entirely on practical decision factors. Nodes 2-6 map directly to the decision criteria mentioned in the understanding (problem type, information freshness, data availability, cost/latency/maintenance, accuracy/traceability) and are MECE-ish with low overlap. I added a "combine both" node because it's a real and common answer to this specific question, and a final checklist node to make the outline actionable for a real decision. I excluded implementation details, tooling/vendor recommendations, deep technical tutorials, and any history/intro filler per the confirmed understanding.
